subject: Post-call: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification — hosted vs current provider
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification — hosted vs current provider

Hi Alex / Finlytics team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning — good to align on the key latency and streaming requirements for your user-facing search flows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clear test plan.

Call recap (high level)
- Primary goal: match or improve current end-to-end latency SLOs for the search path while lowering per-token cost where possible.
- Target SLAs discussed: p95 end-to-end <= 200ms, p99 end-to-end <= 500ms for short prompts (search/autocomplete).
- Streaming: required for progressive UI (first-token latency matters). You indicated streaming must start within ~150ms for perceived responsiveness and continue chunked.
- Throughput/concurrency: typical peak ~400 req/minute, concurrency range 50-100. Burst scenarios up to ~250 rps for short periods were called out.
- Current provider baseline (what you shared on call): representative p95 ~300ms, p99 ~950ms (end-to-end).

Notes on hosted vs current provider
- Hosted Redwood API: optimized low-latency profile we discussed (batching minimized, KV cache primed) typically achieves p95 in the 60-180ms range and p99 in the 150-350ms range for similar search workloads in our benchmarks; actual numbers will vary by request size, model, and region.
- Key levers to hit your target: disable/limit batching for the search route, enable streaming-first-token flush, primed KV cache for common prefixes, and a low-latency inference profile on the Dedicated pool if you want reserved capacity.

Action items / next steps
1) Alex: please share the perf report and a lightweight anonymized traffic sample (CSV/ndjson) showing request size distribution and inter-arrival times.
2) Finlytics: confirm exact p95/p99 targets per route (search vs async summarization).
3) Redwood (Marissa / SE team): we will provision a scoped test API key and a short-lived test environment. SE will run a controlled smoke test + 30-minute load run and report p50/p95/p99 (end-to-end), token throughput, and streaming first-byte latency.
4) Proposed timeline: smoke test w/c Aug 2, full test by Aug 6.

Attachments: reference test plan will be shared by Laura (SE) after this thread.

If that matches your notes, I’ll kick off the provisioning and loop in Laura + Aditya from our engineering team to own the technical execution.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0123

Alex — thanks for the file and the clarifications. We’ll proceed as follows:

1) Laura / SEs will own the test plan and will attach the detailed redwood_test_plan.xlsx to this thread (high-level included below).
2) We will provision a scoped test API key (read-limited, IP-restricted) for Finlytics and a dedicated test pool with the low-latency profile. Key will be valid for the test window only.
3) Proposed smoke test: Mon Aug 2 at 10:00 PT — 10-15 minute validation with a single thread of representative requests to validate streaming-first-byte and disable batching.
4) Ramp & full test: Wed Aug 4 09:00-09:40 PT — 30-minute run to capture p50/p95/p99, streaming metrics (first-byte latency, chunk intervals), and throughput under the concurrency profile you provided.

High-level test plan (summary):
- Workload: use the attached anonymized sample from finlytics_perf_report (request size distribution).
- Metrics: end-to-end p50/p95/p99 (client -> Redwood -> model -> response and first-byte streaming latency), token throughput, CPU/GPU utilization, queue times, and per-request kernel latencies.
- Tunables during test: batching disabled for search route, KV cache primed with top prefixes, and low-latency inference profile (no cross-request batching) enabled. We may flip to a cost-optimized profile afterwards for comparison.

I’m attaching redwood_test_plan.xlsx now. Laura — can you confirm test owner and whether we need any additional infra contacts from Finlytics?

Marissa

Alex / Marissa — looping in a few technical details and the concrete test steps from the SE side. I’ll be the test owner and will run the smoke + full run alongside Aditya.

Planned steps
1) Prep (Mon Aug 2)
   - Validate sample traffic (CSV/ndjson) and sanitize PII.
   - Provision scoped API key + test pool.
   - Prime KV cache with top 200 prefixes; confirm model & quantization variant for the run.
2) Smoke test (Mon Aug 2, 10:00 PT)
   - Single-thread validation of streaming-first-byte, confirm chunking/flush interval, and measure first-byte latency.
3) Ramp test (Wed Aug 4, 09:00 PT)
   - Gradual ramp to target concurrency (50 -> 80 -> 120), maintain peak for 10 minutes, then steady 30-minute run.
   - Collect end-to-end latencies (p50/p95/p99), streaming first-byte, per-token latency, and server-side queue times.
4) Post-run analysis
   - Produce a report with observed p50/p95/p99, tail latencies, and suggested tuning (batching thresholds, kernel selection, and possible Dedicated reservation to stabilize p99).

Technical notes and tuning tips
- For streaming-first-byte, we will use a flush interval of 16-32ms for chat-style chunking; larger chunks can reduce overhead but increase first-token latency.
- We will run with batching disabled for the search route to hit the p95 target; if we see throughput issues, we’ll test a small batching window (1-2ms) and measure tradeoffs.
- If p99 is still high, Dedicated reserved capacity with pinned kernels reduces jitter from multi-tenant scheduling.

Useful links
- Test harness & docs: https://docs.redwood.com/perf-tests
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

I’ll upload the full run results to the Drive folder and share the post-run report. Please confirm the window and provide any infra contacts or allowlisted IPs we should use for the scoped key.

Thanks,
